prompt.query: Determine the equilibrium structure of dioxygen difluoride FOOF (the F-O and O-O bond lengths) and its F-O bond dissociation energy. Species SMILES: FOOF; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase, low temperature. Within the allowed methods, model the system so that it approximates the real conditions stated above as closely as the level of theory permits. Model the process you investigate as a graph and maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root: nodes for every species or electronic state you characterize (with SMILES) and edges for the state changes or transformations between them (with `via` pointing to the TS node id when a transition state was located). Use exactly this JSON shape (key names matter: nodes carry `id`, `role` (one of reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state) and `smiles` (a list of SMILES strings), and may optionally carry a `properties` object for declared quantities; edges carry `id`, `from`, `to`, `via`, `bond_changes` and optionally `barrier_kcal_mol`, `channel` and `favored`): {"nodes": [{"id": "RC", "role": "reactant", "smiles": ["C=O.CN"]}, {"id": "TS1", "role": "transition_state", "smiles": []}, {"id": "P", "role": "product", "smiles": ["..."]}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "RC", "to": "P", "via": "TS1", "bond_changes": {"break": [[1, 2]], "form": [[1, 5]]}, "barrier_kcal_mol": 21.3}]}. A species made of several molecules (a pre-reaction or ion-dipole complex) is ONE node whose `smiles` holds a single dot-joined complex SMILES (like the RC node above), never a list of separate component SMILES; evidence files for such a species must carry that same dot-joined complex SMILES in their `smiles:` annotation. If such a complex is not a clean minimum at the allowed level of theory, still keep the single complex node in the graph, but you may then annotate its evidence files per component species instead (each component with its own `smiles:` annotation). Extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every state you actually characterized. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Declare the equilibrium F-O and O-O bond lengths in Angstrom and the F-O bond dissociation energy in kcal/mol as a structured `properties` object on the reactant species node in mechanism_graph.json, using these unit-carrying keys: `f_o_bond_length_angstrom`, `o_o_bond_length_angstrom`, `f_o_bond_dissociation_energy_kcal_mol`. String values are allowed for descriptive entries. If a particular species or transition state cannot be computed to a trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods, mark the corresponding node or edge "accessible": false in mechanism_graph.json and deliver the rest of the graph as usual; the graph still starts at the reactant complex. The scorer reads that structured flag, not prose; do not declare a number you cannot stand behind. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB, pm7, and B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-SVP; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.
